requirements.text: Ship as one HTML file that runs from `file://` with no network access by default, in tier-1 browsers.

Build with the extended esbuild + inliner pipeline. It produces an IIFE app script, inlined CSS, inert classic worker blocks, gzip+base64 lazy blocks with SHA-256 entries in a build manifest, and notices generated from the metafile.
Enforce size gates: target 8 MB, warn at 9 MB, fail at 12 MB. Report eager, lazy and per-library sizes on every build.
Load every WebAssembly module from inlined bytes. No module may need `eval`/`new Function`. Fail the build if dynamic code evaluation appears outside an allow-list.

Run background work in a persistent pool of classic Blob-URL workers. Each worker's source contains its libraries. The pool has job IDs, priorities, progress, cancel, time-outs, `terminate()` on runaway jobs and transferable buffers. It does not depend on SharedArrayBuffer, WASM threads, module workers or nested workers.
Show running and finished jobs in a Job Queue dock, with progress, cancel and result links.
Read local imagery by byte ranges (`File.slice`, 256 KiB–1 MiB) in workers. Never load a whole multi-GB file into memory.
Keep a separate project file (D1) that references imagery by path and fingerprint, and embeds vectors, graphics, measurements, chains, layouts, settings and small chips.
Relink missing imagery by fingerprint, by folder search and by manual pick. Report any fingerprint mismatch.
In Chromium, save in place and persist file and folder handles. In Safari and Firefox, fall back to download and relink.
Use IndexedDB only as a namespaced crash-recovery journal and a bounded, rebuildable cache. Do not require OPFS on `file://`.
Use one op/transaction store with invertible ops and coalescing for every user edit (vectors, graphics, measurements, layers, chains, DEM edits). Vertex edits must not clone whole geometries.
Provide a project-wide undo/redo history list.
Keep the E2E harness: the built file is tested over `file://`, `http://` and an iframe, with CSP, network capture and WebGL checks.
Handle WebGL context loss and restore all panes without losing state.

Ship a meta CSP with `default-src 'none'`, per-script hashes, `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, `worker-src blob:`, `media-src blob:`, `img-src data: blob:`, and `connect-src` limited to `blob:` plus user-added origins. Never ship `'unsafe-eval'`.
Treat every input file as hostile. Parsers enforce bounds and size limits and run in workers. Malformed input gives an error, never a hang or crash of the page.
Pass HTML from files through DOMPurify. Show SVG from files only as images. Never interpret XML entities from external files.
Read and write the NITF FS*/IS* and ST 0102 security fields. Show top and bottom classification banners and roll up portion marks. Carry the marking in window titles and on products.
Ship an UNCLASSIFIED-only default marking vocabulary. State in About and Help that the tool is not an accredited marking system.
Let the user disable the recovery journal or encrypt it with a session passphrase.
Make no conformance claim for MSP, CSM, JITC NITF, STANAG 3377 or ISM.

Reject GPL, LGPL and AGPL code in the bundle. Keep a notices section for every inlined component, plus attributions for ported code (SARkit, sarpy, GeographicLib) and data (Natural Earth, USGS splib07, EGM96).
Use the tool's own name and icons. Do not copy BAE logos, icons, screenshots or product names.
Provide a Workspace area with Data, Windows and Map views and a Preview pane, beside one or more multiports.

Provide multiports with up to 4 panels (layouts 1×1, 1×2, 2×1, 2×2, 1×3, 2×3). Support new, clone and separate multiport, split/tabbed panels, and drag-and-drop of data from the workspace into a panel.

Provide a Ribbon with the main tabs (File, Home, Select, Draw, Geospatial, Products, View, Add-Ins). Add colour-captioned contextual tab sets (Image, Layer, Surface, Feature, Observation tools) that appear only for relevant layers. Commands keep fixed positions within groups.
Provide a Quick Access Toolbar, an application (File) menu with recent projects, and Ribbon KeyTips on Alt.
Provide dockable, tabbable and floating docks (Layer Manager, ToolBox, tables, logs, properties). Save dock layouts in the project.
Provide a mini toolbar and context menus on right-click, galleries with live preview, and tooltips with cue-card text.

Provide a two-row near-black status bar. It shows cursor lat/lon (DMS or decimal), MGRS on demand, elevation with the terrain source (green or red cell), CE/LE, the math model and the CRS/vertical datum. Cells can be chosen by the user. GSD and NIIRS cells are optional.

Implement the GXP mouse grammar. Middle-button roam with distance-proportional speed; wheel zoom about the cursor; Shift+wheel for Z in stereo or 3D; glove pan; double-click centre and zoom; Esc ends a tool; a double-click makes a tool "sticky".

Provide a default hot-key map (F5 marker, F7 full roam, W whole scene, 1:1, Space pan zone, Q reset 3D camera, arrow keys for magnifier/porthole) and a Customize Hot Keys dialog. Remap or focus-capture chords that browsers reserve (for example Ctrl+T).
Offer an "Exploitation fullscreen" mode with Keyboard Lock in Chromium.
Provide a searchable Preferences tree with User and Common tabs and a lock column.
Generate the theme from `data/ui-tokens.json`, with the GXP-grey (default), derived-dark and print palettes (D2). Move all colours and icons to tokens and `currentColor`.
Mark the active panel with a yellow outline and the active layer with a yellow row highlight. Show a leading asterisk on unsaved layers.
Make dialogs follow one form pattern: grey body, section rules, "…" browse buttons, and Help/Reset/Apply/OK/Cancel.
Provide context-sensitive help: an offline help panel with a page per tool, opened by F1.
Meet the WCAG 2.2 AA baseline for all chrome (keyboard reach, focus order, contrast in all themes, ARIA on docks and Ribbon).
Support high-DPI displays and a UI scale preference. Draw graphics in device pixels.
Provide a Layer Manager with visibility, order, active/master layer, opacity, the "(M,S)"-style role suffix, grouping and per-layer properties.
Provide an Image List tool: a sortable table of loaded images with key metadata, acquisition date and footprint toggle.
Use the browser's native spell check in all free-text fields (labels, report text, attributes).
Load delimited ASCII point files (lat/lon/name/attributes) as point layers through a column-mapping dialog.
Show the Map view with an embedded Natural Earth basemap (1:110m vectors and a low-resolution relief raster). Let the user switch to added online basemaps (Map Backgrounds).
Render all panes in one shared WebGL2 context, with per-pane viewport and scissor (D3).
Store pixels in native integer textures (R8UI/R16UI/R16I/R32F) and filter in the shader with nearest, bilinear, bicubic (default) and Lanczos-3 kernels. Keep raw DN values until DRA.
Use COG overviews, NITF R-sets and JPEG 2000 resolution levels when present. Otherwise build pyramids in workers. Cache 512² tiles with a gutter under an LRU GPU budget.
Implement the image chain in the stage order of `04` §2.2: geometry → spatial filters → DRA/stretch → tone → colour → compare. Record it as JSON in the project, chips and measurement rows.
Provide the SIPS-style DRA (Pmin, Pmax, Emin/Emax modifiers) with full-image, viewport and AOI scopes and Lock DRA. Defaults are 0.02/0.98/0.2/0.4.

Provide the GXP histogram stretches, tonal transfer curves, brightness/contrast/gamma/saturation/sharpness sliders, invert, pseudo-colour LUTs, and a histogram widget with a piecewise editor. Fold all point operations of a band into one 65,536-entry LUT.
Choose a first-display chain by sensor type and bit depth (automatic enhancement). Allow one-click reset or removal of chain steps.
Provide convolution filters (unsharp mask, Laplacian sharpen, edge, smooth, median), morphological filters and a 5×5 MTF compensation kernel slot. CLAHE is a Should.
Provide RGB band selection and composites with per-band stretch. Provide transparency threshold and clip-pixel controls.
Provide Brovey, fast IHS, IHS-NIR and Gram-Schmidt pan-sharpening in real time. PCA is a Should, Ehlers a Could.
Provide the zoom ladder, zoom to box, whole scene, 1:1, zoom about the cursor, and full-roam (mouse) and pan-zone modes.
Provide sensor-native, north-up, up-is-up and shadows-down rotation, computed from the sensor model at the view centre. Free rotation and a load-time preference are included. Heading-up is a Should.
Provide Jump to Point with any coordinate format (REQ-GEO-07). Provide 2D and 3D bookmarks.
Provide a magnifier with power and size controls, an overview with footprint and snail trail, and panel-in-panel.
Link panels by geo-link or pixel-link with per-property selection (centre, scale, rotation, chain) through a Link Manager.
Show roam and ground cursors in linked panes, with configurable shape and colour.
Remove void pixels, honour NITF masks and no-data, and draw raster footprints in the map.
Merge multiple image segments and image collections into one logical image where the NITF attachment levels allow.
Provide a Pixel Matrix Viewer that shows raw DN values around the cursor for all bands.
Draw a north arrow, sun-azimuth and sensor-azimuth arrows, a scale bar (valid at the view centre) and a map grid (lat/lon, UTM, MGRS).
Provide porthole, swiper, flicker (with rate control), blend and two-colour multiview (date 1 red, date 2 cyan) with a date legend, at ≥ 30 fps at 2k.
Record flicker animations to WebM and GIF.
Provide shape tools (point, line, polyline, polygon, rectangle, ellipse, circle, arrow, text, callout), markers, ground-truth shapes, sequence (numbered) graphics, count graphics and icon drawers.
Anchor graphics in ground, image or screen space, with ground as the default. Provide line, fill and transparency styles, a Common Properties window, flip, and copy/paste at the cursor.
Provide autolabels: fields filled from metadata and measurements, with fallbacks. Provide Auto Map: a footprint map inset generated for a product.
Save and load graphics layers as files (GeoJSON and KML/KMZ), keeping styles.
Provide a feature legend for graphics and vector layers, and AOIs usable as processing scopes.
Detect software rendering and fall back to bilinear, with a status warning.

Keep a Mensuration Log dock. Each row holds value, units, method, sensor model, height source, chain, CE90/LE90 (absolute or relative) or "error not available", the σ inputs, and a timestamp. Export it as CSV and JSON.
Provide point position, bracket, range and bearing (true azimuth by default; grid and magnetic optional), polyline length and polygon area/perimeter. All are geodesic on WGS 84.
Measure mono height by shadow (with sun azimuth/elevation guide lines) and by layover/displacement (with sensor geometry guide lines).
Provide targets with range rings, and a Target Table that can be exported.
Track the cursor continuously in ground coordinates, with the elevation source, in the status bar and in an optional readout window.
Compute exact CE90/CE95 from the 2×2 horizontal covariance by quadrature, LE90 as 1.6449 σ_v and SE90 from the 3×3 covariance. Show the error-budget panel with every σ and the Jacobian path.
Tag each result as absolute or relative. Relative results use the cross-covariance.
Provide medial-axis length/width of a polygon and line centre point.
Provide point-to-point line of sight on the loaded DEM/DSM, with curvature and refraction (k default 0.13) and a profile view.
Use WGS 84 as the only internal datum and HAE as the internal height. Record the WGS 84 realization when the data names one, without transforming between realizations.
Embed the EGM96 15′ geoid with cubic interpolation. Accept a user-loaded EGM2008 2.5′/5′ grid pack (D6).
Show heights as HAE and MSL, each labelled with its model ("MSL (EGM96)"). Convert DEMs to HAE before any sensor-model call.
Inline proj4js with embedded EPSG definitions for the codes in `05` §2.2/§4.1. Read WKT from GeoTIFF, GeoPackage and `.prj`. Web Mercator is display-only.
Use GeographicLib for every distance, azimuth, perimeter and area. State the method in results.

Provide our own MGRS/USNG/UTM/UPS/GARS/GEOREF module, ported from GeographicLib. It truncates output, covers UPS and the Norway/Svalbard zones, and returns the cell centre and size on reverse conversion. It passes every `05` §3.8 test vector.
Parse every coordinate format in `05` §3.7 (DD, DMS, DDM, UTM, MGRS, USNG, GARS, GEOREF). Echo the normalized result before acting. A bare pair is lat, lon unless a preference says otherwise.
Provide a coordinate conversion tool for all formats, with precision control. 12-digit MGRS is labelled non-standard.
Provide ECEF/ENU conversions, with one session ENU origin for 3D work, and compute slant range, ground range and elevation/depression angles.
Embed the leap-second table, convert GPS/TAI to UTC, and display UTC in ISO 8601. Compute the sun position when the metadata lacks it.

Put every sensor model behind one CSM-like interface. Each model provides ground-to-image, image-to-ground at a given HAE, ground and sensor partials, parameter covariance, unmodelled error and a valid height range (D4).
Implement RPC00B (with RPC00A remapping, a stated pixel-centre convention, ICHIPB chip handling and the ERR_BIAS/ERR_RAND error terms) in JavaScript.
Provide generic models: affine, polynomial (1st–3rd order) and a projective model from GCPs, for unsupported imagery.
Show the active sensor model per image, let the user choose between the available models, and show the model in the status bar.
Intersect rays with a DEM by march-and-bisect, return every crossing, and label the one used (D17).
Propagate model and measurement error to every ground point (REQ-MEN-06).
Provide registration: Auto Align (tie-point matching), Glove Align (interactive shift), Quick Align (2-point) and polynomial registration with an RMS report.

Read DTED 0/1/2 (with spacing from the UHL, signed-magnitude posts, void −32767, checksum warning and ACC fields), SRTM `.hgt`, and GeoTIFF/COG DEMs (honouring PixelIsPoint/Area, GDAL_NODATA and VerticalGeoKey).
Record each DEM's vertical datum and convert it to HAE on the fly: EGM96 for DTED/SRTM, EGM2008 for Copernicus. Label NAVD88 "not converted". Tag every surface as DSM or DTM.
Auto-load terrain covering the loaded imagery from a user terrain folder. Show the terrain source in the status bar.
Render hillshade (TSR), colour relief, slope and aspect through WebGL2. Provide worker versions for export.
Provide elevation profiles along a line, with a linked cursor.
Provide a ToolBox-style palette (layer filter, active layer, tools, parameters, cue text) with point, polyline, polygon, 3-point rectangle and circle/n-gon tools, single-use and repeat modes.

Implement drawing modifiers as a staged pipeline. Orthogonal, square, constant elevation, snap and close are Must (R1). Parallel, perpendicular, follow terrain, extend/trim, thin, stream digitise and extrude/walls are Should (R2).
Snap to vertex, edge, intersection, end and ground targets with a screen-pixel tolerance, shape-coded cursors, Snap Guard, and a 3D Z rule.
Square buildings by a dominant-direction line fit in a local metric frame (90° ± 0.1°). A 45° variant is a Should.
Provide vertex move/insert/delete, an Edit Vertices table, split line, split polygon, merge and reshape.
Store features in an in-project feature store: typed-array geometry (lon, lat, HAE) with part offsets and per-vertex provenance, vertex-level ops, and rbush/kdbush/flatbush indexes.
Provide a feature attribute table (sort, filter, edit, zoom to) and a feature query by attribute and location.

Read and write GeoJSON, Shapefile (own writer with Z, `.cpg`, `.prj` and a collision-safe field-name map) and KML/KMZ (togeojson + own writer). Include Z, UTF-8, CRS and a round-trip truncation report.
Write KML absolute altitudes as EGM96 heights and GeoJSON Z as HAE.

Read NITF 2.1 (JBP-2024.1 and MIL-STD-2500C files) and NSIF 1.0 with our own reader: file and image subheaders, all IMODEs, blocking, masks, LUTs, IGEOLO/ICORDS, multiple segments with IALVL/ILOC, graphic/text/DES segments and R-sets.

Decode NITF compression in workers: uncompressed, JPEG C3/M3 at 8 and 12 bits (a forked pdf.js `JpegImage` with default-table injection), and JPEG 2000 C8/M8 (inlined `@cornerstonejs/codec-openjpeg`, 16-bit output, `decodeSubResolution` and per-tile decode). VQ (C4) is a Should.
Decode and encode HTJ2K (JPEG 2000 Part 15) with inlined OpenJPH, and use it as the internal pyramid-cache format.

Parse TREs from `data/nitf-tre-catalog.json` (98 TREs). The 11 MUST TREs (RPC00A/B, ICHIPB, BLOCKA, USE00A, STDIDC, PIAIMC, BANDSB, SENSRB, CSEXRA, J2KLRA and others marked MUST) are in R1; the RSM family is in R2. Apply ICHIPB to RPCs ourselves (GDAL does not). Pass unknown TREs through.
Read GeoTIFF 1.1, BigTIFF and COG with geotiff.js through one tile scheduler for local files and range requests. Read the RPC tag 50844, GDAL PAM `.aux.xml` and world files.

Write GeoTIFF/COG with our own writer (geotiff.js writes only uncompressed strips): 8/16-bit and float32, tiled, Deflate via `CompressionStream`, predictor 2/3, overviews. Write NITF 2.1 chips with security fields that keep the parent RPC00B and add ICHIPB. When writing a new RPC00B, snap offsets and scales before fitting the coefficients.
Read JPEG and PNG with world files, and plain images with manual GCP placement.
Read and write DTED and SRTM HGT (REQ-DEM-01, REQ-DEM-16).
Read and write GeoJSON, Shapefile, KML/KMZ and GeoPackage (REQ-EXT-21, REQ-EXT-22).
Load ASCII and CSV point files (REQ-UI-25).
Build the test fixtures FX-01–FX-12 with generators kept outside the shipped HTML, each with machine-readable truth.
Read the public samples in `Research/samples/` without error as a regression suite.
Export annotated chips as PNG and JPEG, with burned-in banners, caption, north arrow and a scale bar valid at the chip centre. Write a chip record.
Provide JSON product templates with autolabels, fallbacks and the `03` §5 default structure. Template editing covers title, legend, grid, inset, metadata block and marking.
Export PDF (jsPDF or print), rendered in strips under 16 MP per canvas. Products use the same render passes as the screen.
Provide Product Properties (page size, DPI, margins, marking, scale) and save-image options (format, bit depth, georeferencing).
Export KMZ products (image overlay plus graphics).
Write geo-aware JPEG (world file) and GeoTIFF chips.
Provide editable report templates (RECCEXREP/IPIR/SUPIR-style) with mensuration tables, without a STANAG 3377 conformance claim.
Open the app to an interactive shell in ≤ 1.5 s on the reference laptop (eager code ≤ 4.5 MB).
Hold ≥ 60 fps for a 2×2 multiport with DRA and bicubic on an integrated GPU, and ≥ 15 fps for one pane on software rendering.
Show the first tile of a local NITF/GeoTIFF of any size in ≤ 1 s, and keep the UI responsive during decoding.
Answer cursor ground-coordinate and CE90 readouts within one frame.
Keep within the memory budget: GPU textures ≤ 384 MB by default, worker heaps 2–4 × ≤ 400 MiB, and a bounded tile cache. Show memory in an About/diagnostics panel.

Provide a feedback whiteboard: a see-through drawing layer over the whole application. Toggle it with **B**, an Add-Ins Ribbon button and a QAT button that shows the page count. Esc leaves it. While it is open, a key shield stops drawing keys from reaching the application.

Provide the tools Interact (V), Pen (P), Highlight (H), Arrow (A), Rectangle (R), Ellipse (O), Text (T), numbered Pin (N) and Erase (E), with six colours (keys 1–6) and three widths. Shift constrains arrows to 45° and shapes to squares and circles.
Keep a separate 200-step undo/redo for marks (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z). It never mixes with the project undo history.

Capture a page as screenshot + marks + notes. Try tab capture first, then a DOM snapshot, then marks only. The composite MUST include the pixels of the WebGL panes (render-to-capture of the shared canvas).
Stamp the current classification banner at the top and bottom of every captured page, PNG and report, using the highest marking on screen.

Let pins link to application items by stable ID: layers, features, graphics, measurements, panes and Ribbon commands. A linked pin can jump to its item, and it shows a "gone" state when the item no longer exists.

Store with each page: its type (bug, suggestion, question), a summary, per-pin notes, general notes, the reporter, and the context (build ID, pane and image ID, centre lat/lon and MGRS, zoom, rotation, image-chain summary, sensor model, marking, theme, browser).
Provide a Review window with two steps: review pages (edit notes, reorder, delete, copy) and send.

Export feedback as one PNG per page, a self-contained HTML report (images plus a JSON data block), JSON (`kind: "gisworkbench-feedback"`, versioned), a plain-text email body and a clipboard image. Offer Web Share and mailto/Gmail/Outlook drafts. Nothing is sent unless the user clicks Send.
Keep feedback sessions in IndexedDB, keyed by project, outside the project file. Warn when storage is unavailable. Obey the journal-off policy (REQ-SEC-06).
Import a feedback JSON file or HTML report to resume or merge a review.
Add optional triage fields (status, priority, assignee) and filter pages by them.
Turn a page into an undoable observation or annotation linked to its pinned items.
Expose feedback pages to the AI assistant as a read-only tool and a resource. The images are sent only when the user attaches them.
Work in every run mode. When tab capture or downloads are blocked (REQ-HOST-03), fall back to marks over a rendered snapshot and an in-page export panel.
Provide an AI Assistant dock: chat, transcript, attachable context, a tool browser with schema-generated forms and a Proposals panel. AI is off until the user adds a connection.
Provide an AI Connections dialog. The default provider is the Anthropic Messages API, with a custom base URL allowed and a model ID per connection. The default model ID is a build setting.
Enter API keys in a secret dialog. Hold them in memory, or in sessionStorage if the user asks. Never write them to localStorage, the project, products, exports or a self-saved HTML.

Ask for consent before the first request of a session, saying what will be sent (text, metadata, image chips). If any marking above UNCLASSIFIED is present, require a second confirmation that names the marking.
Reach providers only through origins in the CSP `connect-src` list ("add origin → save → reload"). Turn blocked requests into a plain explanation. Log every request in the network log (REQ-SEC-12).

Keep an MCP-shaped registry of tools, resources and prompts over the automation API (REQ-ARC-17). Read tools run directly. Write tools run as a dry run and become Proposals that the user accepts or rejects. A proposal whose basis has changed is marked stale. Auto-apply is off by default.
Run a tool-use loop of up to 16 turns that handles `pause_turn` and refusals and caps each tool result.

Provide GIS tools (`gw_*`): list and open layers, jump to a coordinate, read and set the image chain, create and edit graphics and features, run a mensuration, query features, run extraction and validation, generate a product or report, and read the mensuration log.
Describe the current pane or AOI: send a marked chip and its metadata, and return the answer as a draft observation.
Draft report text (IPIR/RECCEXREP-style) from the mensuration log, observations and chips. The draft keeps portion marks, is editable, and is labelled as AI-drafted.
Explain metadata, TREs and error budgets, and answer help questions using the offline help pages as context.
Provide an offline Prompt Helper: build a copy-paste prompt with context and a strict JSON reply schema (graphics, features, observations), validate a pasted reply, and preview it as a Proposal.
Connect to remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP with bearer or OAuth 2.1 PKCE auth. Support elicitation. Serve sampling only after two confirmations.
Expose the registry as an MCP server through the console API, a postMessage bridge with an origin allow-list, and WebMCP where the browser has it. Writes from outside agents follow the proposal rule.
Record provenance on everything AI produces (connection, model, time). AI never writes a measurement value itself; it can only propose operations that the deterministic engine runs.

Detect the run mode at start-up (file, top-level http(s), same-origin iframe, cross-origin iframe, sandboxed iframe, `srcdoc`). Show it in About/Diagnostics. Turn features on or off by detected capability, never by mode name.
Open files with the File System Access picker when it is allowed. Otherwise use `<input type=file>` and drag-and-drop.
Save in place when allowed, else download. When downloads are blocked, show an in-page export panel (copy to clipboard, open in a new tab) and say why.
Have the build emit, beside the full HTML, a paste-ready embed snippet and short instructions for common hosts, and report the snippet size.
Offer a Lite embed profile: a small loader stub that inflates a gzip payload, sized to the embed-box limits found by S-23.
Keep the tool's own meta CSP when embedded and never relax it. Detect features blocked by the host page and report them.
Run without IndexedDB or localStorage (partitioned or blocked storage), with a visible warning and no crash.
Document the iframe attributes that unlock features (`allow="fullscreen; clipboard-read; clipboard-write; display-capture"`, `allow-downloads`), and degrade cleanly without them.
Ship one artifact: the same built file runs in every mode without a rebuild.
Build every Rust crate for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with SIMD128. Load it from inlined gzip+base64 bytes that are listed with a SHA-256 in the build manifest. Never fetch it.
Generate no dynamic code. The build fails if Rust glue contains `eval`, `new Function` or string timers. Use no threads, SharedArrayBuffer or atomics.

Use a thin, stable ABI: functions over linear-memory buffers (pointer and length), explicit alloc/free, typed error codes with a message. Move buffers to workers as transferables. Pass no JS objects in hot paths.
A Rust panic never takes down the page. The worker pool discards a trapped instance, creates a new one, and reports the error in the Job Queue.
Cap memory per instance (default ≤ 1 GiB in a worker, ≤ 256 MiB on the main thread). Parsers enforce size limits.
Give every exported Rust function a JS or reference oracle. Run differential tests with stated tolerances natively and in the browser in CI.
Fuzz every parser of untrusted input (NITF, TRE, DTED, KLV, TS, 4607, LAS/LAZ, SICD XML) with corpora seeded from `Research/samples/`. Release only with zero open crashes or hangs.
Keep all Rust WASM at ≤ 1.2 MB gzip in total and the eager crate at ≤ 250 KB gzip. Report the size per crate on every build.
Accept only MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib or Unicode crate licences (`cargo-deny` in CI). Generate their notices.
Let the same crate serve small synchronous calls on the main thread (cursor read-outs) and bulk jobs in workers, from one source.
Keep reference paths deterministic across browsers: no relaxed SIMD, and a documented float policy.
